name: stage-takes-what-add-takes

steps.command: mkdir -p src && echo a > src/a.py && echo b > b.txt

steps.stderr: ws-git: cannot stage '/': it is outside the workspace root (/workspace), so it is never committed or merged
ws-git: cannot stage '/': it is outside the workspace root (/workspace), so it is never committed or merged
ws-git: stage takes no '-x'. usage: ws-git stage (<paths> | -A); see 'ws-git help'
ws-git: add takes no '-u'. usage: ws-git add (<paths> | -A); see 'ws-git help'
ws-git: stage needs at least one path, or -A. usage: ws-git stage (<paths> | -A); see 'ws-git help'

summary: stage and add are one verb: -A stages everything modified, a directory (or .) what is modified under it, and an option neither takes is one line naming the verb's synopsis. A path above the root is refused, never read as everything under it.
